Subject: Post-call recap: architecture, SLOs, and next steps

Hi Sophie / Carlos —

Thanks for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side so we have a shared reference before the technical deep-dive:

Summary of pain points (what we heard)
- Production QA and model evaluation jobs experience frequent tail latency spikes that block CI gates.
- Need predictable low-latency for short inference calls (few-hundred-token prompts) used in user-facing tooling.
- Batch scoring windows create high peak throughput needs but can tolerate higher per-request latency.
- Data residency / audit requirements for model inputs and logs.

Stated goals
- Real-time: p95 generation latency <= 120 ms for typical short prompts (~<256 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained baseline ~50 req/s for the real-time service, burst to ~200 req/s during batch windows.
- Maintain an error budget that keeps production fallbacks graceful (no more than 0.5% 5xx).
- Auditability: per-request tracing for first 90 days, retention options for longer.

Model & infra notes from the call
- Primary model family: open LLM family (you mentioned a fine-tuned 13B currently, exploring 70B for higher-quality scoring).
- Expectation to quantize (8-bit/4-bit) where possible if quality permits.
- On-premises data flows for sensitive payloads; control plane can be hosted or private depending on compliance.

High-level deployment options we discussed
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for the real-time tier to hit tight p95 SLOs.
- Separate batch pool with larger batching for throughput & cost efficiency.
- Private control plane (VPC) if you need customer-managed networking + KMS.

Immediate next steps (owners + timing)
1) We (Jonas + Priyom) to deliver a first-pass sizing & SLO worksheet and a one-page deployment topology (by Nov 14). (owner: Priyom)
2) LaunchPad to confirm p95 target (120 ms?) and share current peak load diagrams (owner: Sophie).
3) Schedule technical deep-dive to go through the sizing sheet, kernel/hardware tradeoffs, and a canary rollout plan (proposed: Nov 18).

Attached: launchpad_slo_requirements.pdf — our notes from the call with the initial SLO table.

If any of the bullets above are off, flag them and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll use this as the working agenda for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Hi Sophie / Carlos —

Thanks for the note. I put together a short technical breakdown and an initial sizing worksheet (attached: lpb_sizing_sheet.xlsx) — the high level below so the Nov 18 deep-dive has focus.

Short summary (engineering view)
- Latency drivers: model size, hardware (A100 vs H100), tokenization + context length, and network egress between app and inference pool.
- For short prompts (~<256 tokens) we can reach ~80–140 ms p95 on 13B models on H100 with single-request optimizations; 70B models typically sit ~2–3x higher unless aggressively quantized / kernel-optimized.
- Batching helps throughput but adds tail risk; we recommend separate pools to avoid contention between realtime and batch workloads.

Suggested topology (proposal)
- Realtime pool (low-latency): Dedicated H100-equivalent nodes with persistent KV cache, continuous batching disabled for single-request path, and autoscale buffer of +30% above baseline.
- Batch pool (high-throughput): Larger instance types / multi-GPU with aggressive batching and longer sequence lengths; use pre-warmed containers and scheduled scaling for nightly jobs.
- Control plane: Private VPC + hosted control plane option. If you require strict custody, we can deploy full private control plane.

Sizing & initial commit recommendation (ballpark)
- Realtime: start with 4 H100-equivalent GPUs (handles baseline ~50 req/s with room for 30% buffer at p95 target).
- Batch: 2 x 80GB A100-equivalent GPUs for nightly scoring windows (can consolidate or expand based on measured throughput).
- Canary & rollout: begin with 2-node canary in realtime, 7-day traffic ramp, automated fallback to smaller model variant on SLO breach.

SLO matrix (proposed)
- p50/p95/p99 generation latency targets (realtime): 20 ms / 120 ms / 300 ms
- Throughput: baseline 50 req/s (sustained), burst 200 req/s (short windows)
- Error budget: <= 0.5% 5xx per 30-day window

Attachments included: lpb_sizing_sheet.xlsx, mou_draft.docx — the sizing sheet has the calculator cells and assumptions; the MOU draft lists initial pricing and a reserved-capacity option for Dedicated.

I’ll bring the sizing worksheet and a short benchmark slide to the deep-dive. If you want any additional telemetry (kernel latencies, sequence-length breakdowns), say the word and we’ll capture it before the meeting.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
